chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Abdullah ibn Ja'far and others from Ahmad ibn Hamzah who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan the Third (peace be upon him) about a man who takes out his zakat from one town to another town and allocates it among his brothers (relatives/kinsmen), so is that permissible? He said, 'Yes.'

The Shaykh (peace be upon him) said: If he finds people deserving of it in his town but does not place it among them and sends it to another town, if it perishes, he is liable for it. But if he does not find people deserving of it in his town, so he sends it to another town and it perishes, that suffices for him. As for that which indicates that it suffices for him if he does not find people deserving of it, so he sends it to another town and it perishes, what has been narrated is:
ai.seo_question: Is a person liable for lost zakat if transferred to another town?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between voluntary transfer and necessity-driven transfer of zakat, a key topic in Shia fiqh regarding the distribution of alms. Shaykh al-Tusi elaborates that liability for loss depends on whether the transfer was made to seek better recipients or due to a lack of eligible recipients locally, reflecting the principle of *daman* (guarantee) in financial transactions. This ruling ensures that zakat fulfills its social welfare purpose without imposing undue burden on the payer when local conditions necessitate relocation.
